contexts.text: So that thou doest not thy desire in the day of My holiness... nor findest thy desire ()... The celestial man is such that he does not act from his own desire, but from what is well-pleasing to the Lord, which is his desire.
A tree desirable in aspect () = the perception of truth.
Desirable to give intelligence () = pleasure. AC 209.
The fields of desire ().
The Spiritual Angels... perform for him every office which he can desire in that state. HH 450:2.
To thee is his desire, and thou shalt rule over him () = that charity wants to be with faith... AC 365.
Some longed to know what heavenly joy is...
Ye have carried into your temples My desirable things () = the Knowledges of these things.
They desire nothing more than to transfer their own happiness into others.
As the Intellectual desired the Rational, as offspring, and as it is the part of the desire or affection which is speaking...
The Angel of the covenant, whom ye have desired ().
He shall spoil the treasure of all the vessels of desire ().
Certain Souls... who longed to see the glory of the Lord...
As everyone's desires follow him...
Garments of desires () = genuine truths... Of desires = genuine.
To appetite and relish correspond the desire and affection of knowing truth.

The soul, which is the good of the Rational, gives to desire and to be affected with them; thus the things which are of knowledge and doctrine it introduces by means of the delight which is of desire, and the good which is of affection.
Desirable and delectable things for the Divine Rational. Signified.

Dainties = the delights which are of good and the pleasantnesses which are of truth; the delights which are of good are desirable things, and the pleasantnesses which are of truth are delectable ones; for the affection of good is what desires, and then the affection of truth is what delectates.
When he desires the things of Heaven...
The longing for interior truth. Signified.
The affection and longing for the things which are of marriage love. Signified.
That there is conjugial longing. Signified.
Longing on the part of the affection of external truth... that it may be conjoined. Signified.
Thirst = appetite and longing, thus the affection of knowing and imbibing truth... Hunger = the appetite, the longing, thus the affection of imbuing good.
They had a constant desire and longing to come into Heaven.
This endeavour (on the part of the lymph) corresponds to this desire and longing.
Man has no desire to have Knowledges of this.
Because desiring thou hast desired to the house of thy father () = the desire of conjunction with the Divine good which flows in directly.
His soul longeth for your daughter () = a longing for conjunction with this new Church.
Good has an appetite and longs for truth.
From intense longing he importuned to be admitted into Heaven...
In such a substance there is the endeavour and as it were the longing to perform use.
Thus was represented the nature of the desires of those who are in the province of the seminal vessels.
These goods in act... serve for their recreation; for they are their desires; and it is known that when desires are obtained in act, they are for recreation and life.
Affects those who, from good, are in the desire of knowing truths from the Word.

Spiritual heat... gives to desire, to love, also to be affected; therefore desires, loves, and affections are spiritual heats... When the desires and affections, that is, the loves, increase, the body grows warm in the same degree.
Good longs for truth, and truth for good; and according to the longing and its quality, they are conjoined together. AC 8313:4. AC 8772:2.
With affection, longing, delight, or a holy sigh.
The Angels continually long for those things which are of intelligence and wisdom.

He who is in the desire of imbuing his disposition with such things as are of knowledge, intelligence and wisdom, begins to be in sorrow and suffering when he is withheld from such things, and, like one who is in famine, begins to long to return to his spiritual food.
They come into this (state of evening)... in order that they may have an appetite and long for truths and goods...

This comes from the pleasure and thence the desire. They who are in good, feel pleasure in perfecting good by means of truths... wherefore they long for truths; but they who are in evil, have pleasure in evil and in confirming this by means of falsities, wherefore they long for falsities; and as they long for falsities they are averse to truths.

Genii... scent in a moment what man desires... They were permitted to act into my desires... and unless the Lord had guarded me by means of Angels, they would have perverted them into concupiscences of evil...

Pasture = what supports the spiritual life, which is chiefly scientific truth; this the soul of man longs for, as the body for food... That scientifics and truths support the soul, is evident from the desires of knowing with man.
Good Spirits and Angels are in the continual desire of knowing and of being wise... nor are they recreated, and elevated into the blessedness of their life, until their desires are satisfied.
Longing. Signified.
This is a formula by which the affection, thus the longing of the will is expressed.
The man who, when he lives in the body, longs for Heaven...
This enlightenment falls only into such as long to know truths... for the sake of life and use.
They are in their delight and blessedness when they are doing good to the neighbour, for they long for nothing more.
Even to the desire of the hills of an age () = to mutual celestial love.
(The origin of desires.)
That in the desire there is not good. Signified.
As faces = affections, they also = desires.
If he desires truth from affection, he has pleasantness.
The proprium from which the Angels do not act, is signified by... their not finding their own desire, etc.
He who is in spiritual life, desires his support from such things as are called heavenly meats and drinks.
When man is gifted with good by the Lord, he comes into the desire for truth, and this desire is kindled according to the lack of it.
Temptation attacks that which man loves and desires.
The ardent longing for truth. Signified.
Increase of the longing for truth. Signified.
To thirst = to have an appetite for and to desire, namely, truth.
The desire of knowing truth is here described by to thirst; the desire for truth is signified by I will not send thirst for waters, but for hearing the words of Jehovah.
From an intense longing he importuned to be admitted into Heaven.
As it were a blazing longing to put itself off...
By this was represented the nature of the longings of those who are in province to which the seminal vesicles correspond.
Of this it is said that their most desirable things shall not profit (). AE 587:7, Explained.

That which an evil love breathes is called concupiscence; but that which a good love breathes is called longing... Concupiscence belongs to both the will and the understanding, but is properly of the will in the understanding.
Conjunction is effected by means of the state of desire of speaking with another; hence, in the other life they come together... when they desire it.
The Lord's mercy is predicated towards those who are in the deficiency and yet in the desire of good; and his compassions towards those who are in ignorance and yet in the desire of truth.
Any widow = those who are in good without truth, and still long for truth. AC 9206.
An orphan in the celestial sense, = those who are in good and long for truth. AC 9207.

They who are in good and do not long for truth are not in good... Hence good is Known from the fact that it longs for truth... The longing itself, that is, the affection itself of truth for the sake of life, regarded in itself, is the affection of conjunction; the case with this is as with food or bread, which long for water or wine.
Orphans = those who are in truth and not yet in good, yet long for good; here, those who are in truth but do not long for good... That truths perish with those who do not long for good...

The truths which are conjoined with good, in themselves always have the desire of doing good, and are at the same time thereby more closely conjoined with good; or, what is the same, they who are in truths always long to do good, and thus conjoin it with their truths; wherefore, they who believe themselves to be in truths, and do not long to do good, are not in truths...

The salt of the earth = the truth of the Church which longs for good; the infatuated salt = truth without the longing for good... To long for good is to long to do what is good, and thus to be conjoined with good.

To be salted with fire = the longing of good for truth; and to be salted with salt = the longing of truth for good; salt without savour = truth without the longing for good; to have salt in themselves = that longing.
Salt = truth longing for good; and infatuated salt = the truth which is without the longing for good.
That in every offering there was to be salt = that there was to be in all worship the longing of truth for good, and of good for truth.
Salt = the longing for conjunction.
When the one longs to be reciprocally conjoined with the other, that is, good with truth and truth with good, they mutually regard each other.
The reason salt = the longing for truth. Explained.
The instruction of those who are in ignorance of truth, and still are in the longing to learn. Signified.
The needy = those who are in ignorance of truth, and still are in the longing to learn.
Their longing and life. Signified.

Soul, when predicated of those who long to be instructed in the truths of faith, who are signified by sojourners, = longing and life; for soul = life from faith; and longing is the activity itself of life; for it is from the affection of good, and the truth of faith lives from the affection of good.

Salt = the longing of truth for good; the going forth of the waters = the Natural of man which receives the Knowledges of truth and good, and which is amended by means of the longing of truth for good... This amendment takes place, when, from such a longing, the Natural of man receives truths from the Word.
This (enlightenment) takes place according to the quality of the longing for truth with man; and the longing for truth with him is according to his love.

Salted = the longing of truth for good; (for) salt = the longing which is of the love of truth for good... The reason there ought to be the longing of truth for good, is that this longing is conjunctive of both; for in proportion as truth longs for good, it is conjoined with it... Wherefore, when there is the longing for this conjunction in Divine worship and in each and all things of it, there is Heaven in each and all things therein. Signified.

When it is known that salt = the longing for the conjunction of truth and good, it may be known that... everything must be salted with fire = that everyone must long from genuine love; every sacrifice must be salted with salt = that the longing from genuine love must be in all worship; salt without savour = a longing from some other than a genuine love; and to have salt in themselves = the longing of truth for good.
Infatuated salt = a longing from proprium, thus from the love of self and the world; such a longing is the infatuated salt, not fit for anything.
That in all worship there must be the longing of truth for good. Signified.
Longing is the very ardour itself of love, thus its Continuous, and love is spiritual conjunction.
As the longing of truth for good conjoins, so the longing of falsity for evil disjoins, and that which disjoins also destroys. Signified.
To find his desire () = to live according to the delights of their loves.
Wherefore the Angels long for nothing more, than that new Angel guests may come to them.
It is for this reason that in the Spiritual World one is made present with another, provided he longs intensely for his presence.

When anyone is going from one place to another... he comes there more quickly when he longs, and more tardily when he does not long; the very way itself is lengthened and shortened according to the longing, although it is the same. DLW 74.
As wisdom perfects the Angels... all there long for it...
He longs and has an appetite for these things solely because it is truth and because it is good.
Each has as many little children as she yearns for from spiritual storge.

It is there increased... but within the degree of the affection and longing for truth and its good, and not beyond it; they who have had but little affection and longing receive little... but they who have had much affection and longing receive much; the degree itself of affection and longing is as the measure... The reason is, that the love, to which belong the affection and the longing, receives all that agrees with itself. Signified.
They long for truth, and, from the longing, seek it...
The poor = those with whom these Knowledges are deficient, and yet they long for them. HH 420.
The poor man who... desired to be filled with the crumbs... () = the gentiles, who had not the Knowledges of good and truth, and yet longed for them.

They are in ecclesiastical things in Heaven who in the world had loved the Word, and from longing had sought for the truths therein... for the sake of the use of life; these, according to the love and longing for use there, are in enlightenment and in the light of wisdom...
In proportion as these, from the longing of love, investigated the laws of what is just... they are in the capacity of administering offices in Heaven...
When such have longed to know what heavenly joy is... HH 409:end.
All in that World meet, and converse together, when they long to do so...
The Angels... long for nothing more than to perform offices, to instruct, and to convey into Heaven.
There is constantly... the affection of the longing to return to his like, thus to his reigning love.
This conversation the good who were present heard with longing.
They then come into the longing to know what Heaven is like...
They are told... that they can be admitted (into Heaven) if they long for it...
Good is in the perpetual longing and thence endeavour to conjoin itself with truths. References.
He then goes hither and thither, wherever the longings of his disposition carry him.
The natural man can elevate his understanding... to what extent he desires.
The desire of foreknowing future things is connate with very many, but this desire derives its origin from the love of evil.
A few who from the heart long for this influx, sometimes receive some answer...
Presence there is from the recollection of another with the longing to see him.

The fruits of the desire of the soul () = the blessednesses and happinesses of Heaven... These are the desires of men when they are dying, and are also their desires when they newly arrive in the Spiritual World.
The spirit and the bride say, Come = that Heaven and the Church long for the Advent of the Lord.
These long for the light...

It follows, that the one longs for and breathes conjunction with the other. Regarded in itself, love is nothing but a longing and thence an effort for conjunction, and marriage love, for conjunction into one.
As this capacity and longing for conjunction into one is in every single thing...
The states of this love are... a mutual longing of the disposition and the heart to do everything good to the other. General article.
This mutual longing... is of the body from these things.
Especially by accommodations to desires...
For those who long for love truly conjugial, the Lord provides similitudes...
They immerse the interior desires of their mind in their proprium.
New desires which are of good and truth in place of cupidities...
The very desires themselves are continuations of such loves; also cupidities, which are desires in the natural mind, from which this mind is called the disposition.
Appetite is said of the body; to desire, or cupidity, is of the disposition; to long, or longing, is of the interior or rational mind...
Whatever it was given him to long for in thought, they gave him...
They would then have all that they had ever desired... for it is given by the Lord to desire those things which are suitable.

He then began to long... to come into Heaven. It was said to him that if he longed for this, it is permitted; for whatever anyone longs for is granted; and that all consociation is according to the affections, thus according to the desires, for these are affections... He said that he longed to be loosed from the Society in which he was... Then he was loosed, according to his desire... He said that he longed for a good Society... this also was conceded... but he could not remain there... Hence it may be evident... that a Society is allotted according to the desires of a man's life which he has acquired in the world...
Ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man ().

Affliction = anxiety from a longing to Know truths... The reason is, that they are conjoined with the Angels of Heaven, and these continually long for truths, because they long for intelligence and wisdom; they long for these as a starving man does for food... This longing is also in man from early childhood, because he is then conjoined with Heaven, and this longing comes from Heaven; but it perishes with those who turn themselves to the world.
Such are they who are only in natural affection and thence longing.
Desirable things of goods () = the derived truths and goods, which are Knowledges from the sense of the letter.
Desirable things of the eyes () = all things which are of intelligence and wisdom.
To vivify in famine = to give spiritual life according to the desire; the desire for the Knowledges of truth and good is the spiritual affection of truth...
My soul longeth... towards the courts of Jehovah (). AE 1082:4.
God desireth to dwell in it ().
He scattereth the peoples, they long for wars () = the subjugation of the Hells.
All our desirable things are become a waste ()... Desirable things, in the Word, = the truths of the Church.
More desirable are they than gold (). What is desirable = that which is of affection and of love.
Many just ones and prophets have desired to see what ye have seen ().
To long for wars = ratiocinations against truths.
Occurs. AE 781:16.
Thy servants have desired her stones ().
Desirable in aspect () = that which the understanding desired.
The desires of your father ye will do () = that they wanted to be in the evils of their cupidities.
Woe to those who desire the day of Jehovah (). As they believed that He would deliver them from their earthly enemies, and carry them into glory... they desired Him...
The goods which are in the natural mind from the spiritual, are called affections and desires for these things.
Desirable things, in the Word, are said of truths.
He hath desired it... Here will I dwell, because I have desired it ().
My soul desired the earliest (). Explained.
They desire the approach of God ().
My flesh longeth for Thee () = man as to the good of the will.
The fruits of the desire of the soul = the gladnesses and joys which have been awaited from worship and life according to the traditions of the Babylonish religion.
